beats.head: Brunstone & Sons Idles Vault II Lines and Cuts 1,400 Jobs After Demand Shortfall
beats.body: Reversing last quarter's triumphant capacity doubling, Dagny Frost announced Brunstone will mothball two of its four Vault II lines and eliminate roughly 1,400 positions to realign output with tepid orders. The company took a $320M restructuring charge and withdrew full-year guidance, with Frost conceding the expansion had 'run ahead of the market.' The whiplash from her earlier 'recovery complete' declaration drew sharp criticism from the board.

beats.head: Calderforge Reports First Stable Yields at Stormwell Hall Four Under Vann
beats.body: In her first major update, Perra Vann said the long-stalled fourth Stormwell hall has reached stable production yields for the first time, clearing a milestone that had eluded the prior regime. Vann reported the hall is now running at 60% of target capacity and expects full ramp within two quarters, though she cautioned demand recovery lags the fix. The news marks the first tangible progress in Calderforge's turnaround.

beats.head: Greenmarsh Agro Tops Estimates as Second Blending Line Lifts Output
beats.body: Petra Kessler's Greenmarsh delivered a slight beat as its newly commissioned second blending line pushed soil-blend volumes up 8% quarter-over-quarter. The distribution pact continued to feed steady bundle demand across two regions, and management nudged full-year guidance modestly higher. Kessler reiterated her preference for measured, long-horizon growth.

beats.head: Halhold Systems Ousts Marcus Thorne as Losses and Payout Weigh
beats.body: The Halhold board removed Marcus Thorne after a third consecutive miss and mounting fallout from the $2.1B reliability payout, naming reliability-engineering chief Ines Corvalan as chief executive. Corvalan pledged to stabilize Compute yields and rebuild customer trust, warning that a return to growth remains 'several quarters out.' The shakeup ends Thorne's turbulent tenure that began just last year.

beats.head: Kessel Drive Unveils Vanta Ultra Pack With 20% Range Gain
beats.body: Riding the momentum of recovered cell volumes, Aldric Venn took the stage in Corvin Bay to launch the Vanta Ultra, a storage pack Kessel Drive claims delivers a 20% range improvement at a 12% lower cost per kilowatt-hour. Venn promised first deliveries within two quarters and touted pre-orders from three fleet operators, though he offered no firm figures. Analysts noted the aggressive timeline mirrors Venn's pattern of headline-first announcements.

beats.head: Marrowcyon Stretches Streak to Eighth Straight Quiet Beat
beats.body: Theo Orne's Marrowcyon posted another modest beat, edging estimates by two cents as apparel volumes ticked up 3% and fixtures held flat. Management reaffirmed its unchanged full-year outlook and again declined to hold a call, letting the numbers speak. The uneventful result extended one of the sector's steadiest runs.

beats.head: Thronehaus & Co. Acquires Meridian Dial Works to Secure Complications Talent
beats.body: Cora Dray struck again, agreeing to buy specialist movement house Meridian Dial Works for a reported $180M to bring perpetual-calendar and tourbillon expertise in-house. The deal folds Meridian's 40-person atelier into the Aurel program and secures a supply of complications Thronehaus had previously sourced externally. Dray framed the purchase as 'vertical craftsmanship,' extending her long record of acquisitive expansion.

beats.head: Tillage & Co. Logs Another In-Line Quarter as Input Demand Holds
beats.body: Kestrel Fenn's Tillage & Co. reported results squarely in line with expectations, with farm-input volumes flat and margins unchanged from the prior period. Management characterized the quarter as 'exactly what we planned' and left guidance untouched. The dependable print continued the house's long, unflashy streak.

beats.head: Bruncrest Works Beats Again as Second Compute Line Clears Aria Ultra Backlog
beats.body: Bruncrest posted revenue of $1.9B for the quarter, up 34% year-over-year, as the second compute line drew the Aria Ultra backlog down from $5B to $4.1B. Ines Marlow told the call that yield on the new line hit target six weeks ahead of plan, though she cautioned that margins would tighten as ramp costs peak next quarter. Order inquiries beyond Aria Ultra rose sharply.

beats.head: Carrowcyon & Sons Unveils Ambient Series to Broaden Smart-Dimming Beyond Homes
beats.body: Cole Brandt introduced the Ambient Series, a commercial-grade smart-dimming range aimed at offices, hospitality and retail floors, priced roughly 20% above the flagship residential line. The launch leans on the three-line capacity buildout completed last quarter, with early pilot installs booked across four regional hotel chains. Management framed the move as a natural extension of demand that has consistently outrun consumer supply.

beats.head: Greywater Grid Sued by Compute Partner as Discharge Scandal Triggers $2.4B Pact Dispute
beats.body: The anchor customer behind Greywater's $2.4B closed-loop supply pact filed suit to void the agreement, citing the leaked memos showing overstated discharge figures as a material misrepresentation. The complaint seeks the return of $310M in prepayments and damages, and names Sable Renwick directly. Renwick called the claims 'opportunistic' but confirmed outside counsel has been retained and that two smaller site contracts are now under review.

beats.head: Gromford Works Tops Estimates as Emblem Timepieces Lift Margins
beats.body: Gromford beat expectations with revenue up 22%, driven by the Emblem timepiece extension and the global department-chain rollout reaching 140 storefronts. Halvard Pryce said timepieces carried a gross margin roughly eight points above the fine-goods average, boosting overall profitability. Pryce signaled a limited-edition Emblem release timed for the coming holiday window.

beats.head: Halhold Works Issues Full Recall of Aveline Successor as Battery Probe Widens
beats.body: Anselm Rocha announced a complete recall of the Aveline Successor device line after regulators linked the earlier heating reports to 41 confirmed thermal incidents, including three minor injuries. The recall covers an estimated 620,000 units and is expected to cost between $180M and $240M, effectively erasing the reset program's early sales gains. Rocha said shipments would halt until a redesigned battery module is certified, a delay of at least two quarters.

beats.head: Ornewright Supply Adds National Grocer to Cold-Chain Network Ahead of Vellhorn Opening
beats.body: Rhys Throne signed a three-year cold-chain distribution agreement with a national grocery group, projected to add $190M in annual food-service and farm-input volumes. The deal is structured to draw on the forthcoming Vellhorn hub, which remains on schedule to open next quarter. Throne said combined Dunmere and Vellhorn capacity would cover the new commitments with room to spare.

beats.head: Castlestone Lands Landmark Grid-Core Compute Contract in Karsh Comeback
beats.body: Castlestone secured a $2.1 billion, multi-year Grid-Core compute supply agreement with the Vantor Industrial Group, its largest deal ever and a striking reversal from last year's guidance cut. CEO Pell Karsh, who cut 1,800 jobs and split the Grid-Core unit during the reset, called it 'vindication for the hard calls.' The award sent management to raise full-year revenue guidance for the first time since the restructure.

beats.head: Castlehold Ordered to Halt Second Plant as Probe Escalates and Framework Delivery Slips
beats.body: Regulators widened their investigation into Castlehold's grid-storage incident, ordering a full shutdown of the second plant pending a design review and citing 'systemic containment concerns.' The halt jeopardizes near-term deliveries under the company's flagship $2B framework, and CEO Halden Voss acknowledged 'material schedule risk' while insisting the underlying technology is sound. Two customers have requested contract reviews.

beats.head: Marrowstone Build Wins $780M Coastal Rail Corridor, Its Largest Single Award
beats.body: Marrowstone Build secured a $780M design-and-build package for the first phase of a coastal freight rail corridor, its biggest single contract on record and enough to push backlog beyond $2.1B. CEO Delphine Vaugh said the win 'changes the scale of what we can bid on' and confirmed the company is expanding its heavy earthmoving fleet to service the multi-year program. Work is slated to begin next quarter.

beats.head: Vossenspire Holdings Splits Compute and Power Units in Vok's Post-Probe Overhaul
beats.body: New CEO Maren Vok unveiled a sweeping restructure that separates Vossenspire's compute operations from its troubled Power & Storage arm, with a $610M charge tied to the shuttered storage-bank program. Vok said the split lets the company 'ring-fence the past and fund the future,' pledging to exit the facilities named in the resolved regulatory probe. The plan cuts roughly 1,400 roles across the storage division.

beats.head: Woldmark's Meridian Doubles Throughput in Landmark Benchmark as Sonn Declares Comeback
beats.body: Woldmark disclosed independently verified results showing its Meridian compute modules deliver 2.1x the sustained throughput of the retired Halcyon line at comparable power draw. CEO Petra Sonn, never shy of a headline, called Meridian 'the machine that erases the last two years,' and confirmed three unnamed hyperscale customers have moved to full production orders. The results mark the first clear technical vindication since the Halcyon 4 collapse.

beats.head: Lhaus Industries to Acquire Battery Maker Kellstrom for $2.1B in Push Into Power & Storage
beats.body: Cole Brandt unveiled the $2.1B cash-and-stock purchase of Kellstrom, a maker of grid and vehicle storage cells, in the largest deal of his seven-decade run atop Lhaus. The move vertically links Kellstrom's cell output to Lhaus's Power & Storage unit and its platform vehicle line, though it lifts the company's debt load to a decade high. Brandt called storage 'the next platform' and said Kellstrom's two plants would run under Lhaus branding by year-end.

beats.head: Blackhold Hit With Investor Suit Over Storage Fleet Defect as Losses Mount
beats.body: A consolidated shareholder suit filed against Blackhold alleges executives understated known thermal risks in the storage fleet ahead of the recall, seeking damages exceeding $1.4 billion. The complaint names CEO Halden Dabney directly and cites internal design reviews from before the first overheating incident. Blackhold said it would contest the claims, but disclosed the recall and remediation have already cost $780 million.

beats.head: Brunstone & Sons Misses Badly as Vault II Capacity Ramp Outpaces Demand
beats.body: Just one quarter after declaring the recovery 'complete,' Brunstone reported a steep earnings miss as the doubled Vault II line ran well below breakeven utilization, forcing a $210M inventory writedown. Dagny Frost conceded the capacity expansion 'moved faster than the order book,' and the company withdrew its prior full-year targets. The fleet supply pact remains intact but its volumes fell short of ramp assumptions.

beats.head: Regulators Widen Marlgear Supply Probe to Full Device Line as Kessel Fault Scandal Deepens
beats.body: Regulators escalated their inquiry into Marlgear Supply, expanding the Kessel fault investigation to cover the company's entire Devices catalog after new filings suggested the destroyed records touched multiple product families. New CEO Halvard Renn pledged full cooperation and voluntarily suspended shipments of three Kessel-based lines pending review. The widened probe threatens roughly a third of Marlgear's device revenue.
